item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Sharpen a Blurry Dog Photo

turns.text: This phone pic of my dog came out blurry. Can you make it clearer and bigger, 640 pixels on the long side? Keep it looking natural.

item.tests: Enhances a blurry supplied photo rather than replacing its subject or merely enlarging the blur.

answer_sheet.Enhancement style: Natural-looking blur reduction and sharpening, not a stylised remake.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: 640 pixels on the long side; preserve the original proportions and framing.
answer_sheet.Subject and background: Keep the same dog, pose, expression, and background.

must_haves: The same golden retriever from blurry-dog.jpg remains recognisable in the same pose.
The dog's visible contours and facial features are clearer than in the blurry source.
Fur and edges look natural, without pronounced sharpening halos or invented decorative detail.
The background and full original framing are preserved.
The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.

turns.text: This phone pic of my dog came out blurry. Can you make it clearer and bigger, 640 pixels on the long side? Keep it looking natural. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—though the blur is strong, so AI may reconstruct some fur and facial detail rather than recover the original detail exactly.

**Lowest-cost AI option:** one edit with the free-plan **Flux 2 Klein**, at **640 pixels on the long side**, requesting gentle deblurring and a natural look while preserving your dog, pose, and background.
- **Listed starting cost: 5 credits per image.**
- I can’t verify the exact charge or your remaining balance with the tools available here, so I won’t start it without your approval.

**Cheaper alternative:** ordinary resizing and light sharpening in a photo editor costs **no Magic Hour credits**. It can enlarge this 512 × 512 photo to 640 × 640, but won’t restore much missing detail. A smaller AI output isn’t listed as cheaper, and “shorter” doesn’t apply to a still photo.

**Nothing has been run or charged.** Would you prefer instructions for the no-credit option, or the AI edit once its exact cost can be confirmed?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the no-credit resizing and light sharpening instructions.

turns.agent:
You can do this in a free editor such as **Photopea**, which runs in your browser—no Magic Hour credits needed.

1. Open **photopea.com** and choose **File → Open** to load your dog photo.
2. Choose **Image → Image Size**.
   - Keep the aspect ratio locked.
   - Set the width to **640 px**; the height should also become **640 px**.
   - Use **Bicubic** resampling, then click **OK**.
3. Choose **Filter → Sharpen → Unsharp Mask**. Start with:
   - **Amount:** 40%
   - **Radius:** 0.7 px
   - **Threshold:** 3
4. View the image at **100% zoom** and toggle the preview. If bright outlines appear around the dog or the grass looks crunchy, lower the amount to **20–30%**.
5. Choose **File → Export As → JPG**, use **90–95% quality**, and save a new copy.

**Keep expectations modest:** this will make the picture larger and slightly crisper, but it won’t recover the fur or facial detail lost to the strong blur. Gentle sharpening will keep it looking most natural.
